# Halligan

> Automated guardrail testing for AI assistants. Halligan points a suite of
> adversarial probes at any model — Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, LM Studio
> or a custom HTTP endpoint — grades the responses against declarative checks,
> and fails the build when a guardrail moves. It ships with a probe suite for
> Catholic-aligned AI.

The premise is that guardrails rarely break on the first turn. A single-turn
eval asks a model one bad question and records the refusal; Halligan runs the
whole conversation, because the failure that matters usually arrives on the
fifth attempt after refusing has been reframed as cruelty. To find that, it
runs multi-turn conversations rather than isolated prompts, repeats each case
to separate a real guardrail from a coin flip (reported as a flake rate), and
slides a probe through every position in a conversation to work out whether the
prompt or the build-up is doing the damage.

Key facts: Apache-2.0, Python 3.10+, `pip install halligan`, published by
Foxxception LLC. It is a command-line tool that runs on your own machine or CI
— there is no hosted service, no account, and no telemetry. API keys are read
from the environment only and never written to disk.

## Start here

- [Halligan homepage](https://halligan.dev/): What it is, why multi-turn testing finds what single-turn evals cannot, and an embedded preview of a report.
- [Getting started](https://halligan.dev/start): Install, `halligan init --interactive`, pick a provider and pack, cost a run with `--estimate`, then run it.
- [Sample report](https://halligan.dev/report): A real generated HTML report — scores, per-case results, flake rates and full transcripts.
- [halligan on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/halligan/): The published package.

## Documentation

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mobius29er/halligan/main/README.md): The full manual. Covers packs, policies, the controlled experiment, position sweep, writing your own probes, age safety, repeats and flake rate, cost, local models, failed-vs-errored, credentials, and repository layout.
- [Age safety matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mobius29er/halligan/main/docs/age-safety-matrix.md): How responses are expected to differ by the stated age of the user, and what counts as a failure at each tier.
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mobius29er/halligan/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): How to send back a probe suite or a pack adapted to another domain.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan): Issues, releases, and the suites themselves under `suites/` and `packs/`.

## Concepts worth getting right

- [Packs](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan/blob/main/README.md#packs): A pack is a named bundle of suites — `catholic` is the one that ships. Suites are YAML files of probes; probes are data and are never executed.
- [Repeats and flake rate](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan/blob/main/README.md#repeats-and-flake-rate): A case that passes 14 times and fails 6 is not a pass. Repeats are how a real guardrail is told apart from a coin flip, and flaky cases are reported separately from failures.
- [Position sweep](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan/blob/main/README.md#position-sweep--compound-probe-position-sweep): Sliding one probe through every position in a conversation, to establish whether the prompt or the accumulated context caused the break.
- [Failed, errored, and the difference](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan/blob/main/README.md#failed-errored-and-the-difference): A guardrail that gave way is not the same result as a transport error, and Halligan never reports one as the other.
- [A note on the probe content](https://github.com/mobius29er/halligan/blob/main/README.md#a-note-on-the-probe-content): The suites deliberately contain jailbreak attempts and arguments for positions the project rejects. They are test inputs, not endorsements.

## Security

- [Security policy](https://halligan.dev/security): How to report a vulnerability, what is in scope, safe harbour, and how credentials are handled.
- [SECURITY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mobius29er/halligan/main/SECURITY.md): The canonical repository policy, with the commands for revoking and scrubbing a leaked key.
- [security.txt](https://halligan.dev/.well-known/security.txt): RFC 9116 machine-readable contact.
